provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: antecedent witness is the Mame, Tours 1922 (editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam); 85% of the 1962 body's tokens align in order after canon folding; the 1962 writes 'Ianuarii' where the witness prints 'N' at the day's-saint slot; the 1962 writes 'Sociorum eius' where the witness prints 'N' at the day's-saint slot; the Mame prints j where the 1962 prints i (Iesum/Jesum, eius/ejus) and its recogniser renders the ae ligature as 'z' or 'e'; both are orthographic; pointing: the antecedent's reading is recorded verbatim above so its commas and colons can be compared, but its punctuation is NOT safely collatable - the recogniser turns commas into full stops, semicolons and question marks - so no punctuation difference here should be read as a difference between the printings; the 1962 prints the conclusion as 'Per Dominum.'; conclusion length was excluded from the alignment and is recorded here as printed, per the settled rule. Corroboration: Pustet 1862 text-layer lines 101866-101876 (50% coverage); Vatican typical 1604 at line 52046 (45%; degraded, corroboration only); Benziger 1962 conformed printing at line 103239 (75%; comparison only, never a publication basis). Recorded limitation: The antecedent reading is taken from that witness's text layer, not from a page image, so its letterforms are inferred rather than read; only the 1962 target was read on a page. I did not collate the antecedent's Introit, readings, chants or any Secunda Oratio / Alia Secreta / Alia Postcommunio.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui nos annua sanctorum Martyrum tuorum Januarii et Sociorum ejus
solemnitate laetificas: concede propitius; ut, quorum gaudemus meritis,
accendamur exemplis. Per Dominum.

translations.caution: Original study translation; not approved for liturgical use or recitation.
translations.text: God, you gladden us with the yearly solemnity of your holy martyrs Januarius and his companions; graciously grant that we who rejoice in their merits may be set aflame by their examples. Through the Lord.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Oblatis, quaesumus, Domine, placare muneribus: et, intercedentibus sanctis
Martyribus tuis Januario et Sociis ejus, a cunctis nos defende periculis.
Per Dominum.

translations.caution: Original study translation; not approved for liturgical use or recitation.
translations.text: Lord, we pray, be appeased by the gifts we have offered, and, through the intercession of your holy martyrs Januarius and his companions, defend us from every danger. Through the Lord.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Haec nos communio, Domine, purget a crimine: et, intercedentibus sanctis
Martyribus tuis Januario et Sociis ejus, caelestis remedii faciat esse
consortes. Per Dominum.

translations.caution: Original study translation; not approved for liturgical use or recitation.
translations.text: Lord, may this communion cleanse us of sin and, through the intercession of your holy martyrs Januarius and his companions, make us sharers in the heavenly remedy. Through the Lord.
